So the four blocks (IA1_REL / IA2_HBODY / IA3_SOCIAL / IA4_GEN) come straight from the deposit and need no inference. What IS inferred is position 1..5 within a block: the S2 codebook lists the 20 activities as one flat roman-numbered list (i)..(xx) tied to no variable code, and the mapping assumes that list runs in code order. NO data_labels route exists: the S1 .xls was opened and carries no variable labels and no value labels, only the bare ASCII column names. STEP 3b (instrument match): this is the SATISFACTION/preference half, not the frequency half. The 20 live per-item means reproduce the raw IA*_* columns of the workbook to 2dp (e.g. IA1_REL_1 3.093, IA4_GEN_4 3.592) and differ sharply from the paired IA*_TIME columns that built meloni_2015_child_ia_frequency (IA4_GEN_4 4.71, IA3_SOCIAL_3 1.42); the preference means are compressed (2.45-3.59, SD 0.35) with every block's mean of item means within 0.35 of 3, the signature of a within-block ordering constraint, while the frequency means span 1.42-4.71 (SD 0.94). VERIFICATION: Step 5b routes 8 + 2, status PARTIAL, re-runnable as verify_meloni_2015_child_ia_satisfaction.R (VERDICT: PASS). 6/6 a-priori preference predictions hold and 7/7 hold on the paired frequency columns, which share the same code stems and separate items this table's compressed scale cannot. It does NOT separate IA1_REL_2 vs IA1_REL_3, IA2_HBODY_2/_4/_5, IA3_SOCIAL_2 vs _5, or IA4_GEN_2 vs _5. TEXT: text_source=translated_substitute, translation_source=study_supplied. Interviews were conducted by Fabio Meloni in participants' homes in Perugia with 76 Italian primary-school children, so administration was Italian; the whole S2 codebook is English, the S1 .xls holds only numbers and ASCII codes, and S3/S4 are JavaScript assets, so no Italian wording exists in the deposit -- the authors' own English ships in the base fields with language=Italian and empty _translated columns. The items were administered as pictures, so item_text is the codebook's verbal description of each picture. DEVIATIONS FROM LITERAL TRANSCRIPTION, all disclosed: the codebook typo 'read stories form the Bible' is shipped as 'from'; option_text 'liked the least'/'liked the most' expands the source's parenthetical '1 (the least) to 5 (the most)'; resp 2-4 have no label in any source and are left blank. correct_response is blank -- a preference ranking has no key. RIGHTS: no block. Child's Interests and Activities is the authors' own instrument -- the paper keeps Evans' (1998) format (item number, item type, Likert ranges, coding system) but states 'the item content, instructions, and questionnaire stimuli were modified' -- and its wording is published by them in the CC BY 4.0 S2 File ('Copyright: (c) 2015 Meloni et al. ... Creative Commons Attribution License, which permits unrestricted use, distribution, and reproduction in any medium'). itemtext/instrument_rights_register.csv was checked by instrument name and by item wording: no row matches, and no fee, permission-required, non-commercial, no-derivatives or no-redistribution clause is quotable for this instrument anywhere on the article or supplement pages.
public_note: The interviews were conducted in Italian with Italian primary-school children, but neither the article nor its supplements publish any Italian wording, so the item text shown here is the English description of each activity given in the study's own S2 File codebook; the activities were administered as pictures rather than as printed sentences, the within-block order of the item codes was inferred from that codebook's list order, and note that the instructions quoted here cover the whole task and so also name the Never/Once-a-year/Once-a-week card, which scores the sibling table meloni_2015_child_ia_frequency -- this table's 1-5 is the preference ordering, 1 = liked the least, 5 = liked the most

ITEM CODES: S1 File dataset (journal.pone.0128876.s001, .xls, sheet Dataset_S1), columns DEQ1_CE_MD .. DEQ11_CE_ND. Processing script data/meloni_2015_disability.py.

TEXT: S2 File 'Details of Measures, Procedures, and Coding' (journal.pone.0128876.s002, a legacy binary .doc converted with soffice --convert-to txt), section 'Child's Protocol > Disability explanation-closed-ended questionnaire' -- its Instructions paragraph and its 'Statements (n = 11 x 2 masculine and x 2 feminine)' list, transcribed verbatim. The CHILD version was used deliberately: the same S2 file carries a Parent's Protocol version of this questionnaire whose statement (viii) differs ('the world makes him things difficult' vs the child form's 'the world makes him think it is difficult') and whose instructions are entirely different. ITEM CODES: S1 File dataset (journal.pone.0128876.s001, an IBM SPSS Export Facility .xls, sheet Dataset_S1), columns DEQ1_CE_MD .. DEQ11_CE_ND. That file carries NO variable labels and NO value labels -- opened and checked this round, only bare ASCII column names -- so there is no data_labels route for this deposit. DERIVATION: data/meloni_2015_disability.py melts deq_ce_cols by name with no rename, so the IRW item code IS the source column name (core-model pattern 1, no positional step); the child/parent split is by ROW, not by column (is_child = id between 200 and 299, i.e. the codebook's Protocol 201-281), which is how the child version was established -- the columns are shared with meloni_2015_deq_ce_parent. TARGET BLOCKS: MD/SD/CD/ND come straight from those column names and are self-describing against the four stimuli the codebook names -- Giovanni in a wheelchair (motor), Maria blind (sensory), Paolo autistic (cognitive), Elena a normal person (no disability); the S1 column order MD, SD, CD, ND reproduces the codebook's own stimulus order (i)-(iv) exactly, and the 2-male/2-female split of those targets matches the codebook's 'x 2 masculine and x 2 feminine'. WHAT IS INFERRED: the codebook prints the eleven statements as a flat roman list tied to no variable code, so statement (i)..(xi) -> DEQ1..DEQ11 is presentation-order inference. Checked against the data (route 8, verify_meloni_2015_deq_ce_child.R, 7/7 predictions): DEQ10 ('he does not walk well and he does not take the bus') has the largest MD-CD gap of the eleven (1.22; MD 3.03, CD 1.81) and DEQ11 (also mobility wording) the second (1.06); DEQ4 ('he's sick') is 2.84/2.93/2.59 for the three disability targets against 1.51 for the able-bodied one; DEQ6 ('he encounters lots of obstacles') is the top statement for both MD (3.21) and SD (3.13), which the article's Discussion corroborates by name -- it quotes '[Giovanni has difficult in life because] he encounters lots of obstacles' as more agreeable than '[...] he's ugly' (DEQ2_CE_MD 1.49). NOT established: statements 8 and 9 are the same two clauses in reversed order and are indistinguishable (2.92/2.89 MD, 2.55/2.62 SD, 2.52/2.49 CD); 1/2/3 all sit at the floor; 5 and 7 are not separated. Hence PARTIAL. TRANSCRIPTION DEVIATIONS: only the masculine statement set is published, so it ships for the two female-target blocks too (see public_note); typographic apostrophes/quotation marks rendered as ASCII; nothing else altered. option_text<->resp: the codebook's Measures section describes the children's response card as 'four expressive faces indicating either disagreement (1, a lot; 2, a little) or agreement (3, a little; 4, a lot)', which numbers the anchors directly; shipped as Disagree a lot / Disagree a little / Agree a little / Agree a lot (an expansion of that parenthetical form, not a quotation of it; the child instructions' own spoken labels are 'Strongly Agree, Agree, Disagree, or Strongly Disagree'). resp 1.5/2.5/3.5 are the 'intermediate points' the codebook allows and carry no label in any source, so option_text is blank there. correct_response is blank: the instrument measures agreement and has no key. RIGHTS: no block. The instrument is the authors' own -- the article states the questionnaires 'maintained the same format as the questionnaires that Evans [35] used, i.e., item number, item type ..., Likert scale ranges, and open-ended questionnaire coding system. However, the item content, instructions, and questionnaire stimuli were modified' -- so the wording shipped is Meloni et al.'s, published by them in the S2 File of a CC BY 4.0 PLOS ONE article ('Copyright: (c) 2015 Meloni et al. ... Creative Commons Attribution License, which permits unrestricted use, distribution, and reproduction in any medium'). Nothing in itemtext/instrument_rights_register.csv matches (33 rows, checked by instrument name and by item wording); no fee, permission-required, non-commercial, no-derivatives or no-redistribution clause is quotable for it, and there is no external rights holder to consult. STEP 3b: matches. 44 live items named DEQ*_CE_* on resp 1-4 with half points, n = 73-76 per item, exactly the 11 x 4 closed-ended block of the deposit restricted to the 76 child respondents; not one of the five other measures in the same file (DEQ_OE_* is the open-ended counterpart with 0-8 counts, HK*/IA*/PE*/CHIA* are the other four questionnaires).
